AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health and trajectory are genuinely strong: Q2 FY2026 showed +16.6% YoY revenue growth and +21.8% EPS growth, gross margin expanded to 49.3% from 47.1% YoY, operating cash flow grew +19.8% YoY, and the balance sheet has deleveraged dramatically (equity +59.5%, debt -12.8% over 5 quarters). Services revenue hit a record $31B (+16% YoY) with 75%+ gross margins, and the 2.35B installed base with 93% retention underpins the ecosystem moat. However, valuation is not cheap: P/E of 35.8x sits in the lower-middle of the 30.2-43.1x 12-month range, and the 2.8% earnings yield is 167bps below the 10-year Treasury at 4.47%. The stock is near all-time highs at $298.21. Pillar 2 (valuation) is neutral — not expensive vs own history peak of 42x, but not a bargain either. Pillar 3 gets a modest positive bump: the $100B buyback authorization (May 1, 2026), Q3 guidance of 14-17% revenue growth above Street expectations, and the CEO transition signaling continuity are credible near-term fundamental catalysts. Regulatory risk (DOJ antitrust, EU DMA) and China exposure (~18% of revenue) are real but partially offset by $147B liquidity and $62B net cash. Net: strong franchise with accelerating growth, but priced for continued execution with limited margin of safety — mildly to moderately attractive.
